name: Restaurant / Kitchen Brigade System
description: Classical French or modern kitchen brigade combined with front-of-house restaurant operations. Back-of-house runs on a strict hierarchy from Executive Chef down through Sous Chefs, Chef de Partie (line cooks by station), and Commis (apprentices). Front-of-house is led by the General Manager with Servers, Bartenders, and Bussers. The Owner or GM sits at the top, bridging both sides.

org_structure.overview: The restaurant organizational structure is a dual-chain system: back-of-house (kitchen brigade) and front-of-house (service team) operate semi-independently but must coordinate tightly during service. The kitchen follows the classical brigade hierarchy originated by Escoffier, with each Chef de Partie owning a specific station. Modern kitchens may consolidate stations but retain the rank structure. Front-of-house manages guest experience from arrival through departure. The Owner or General Manager sits at the apex, with the Executive Chef and GM as the two senior operational leaders. The structure can flex from a 10-person fast-casual team to a 100-person fine-dining brigade.

departments.name: Executive Leadership / Ownership
departments.description: Highest-level decision makers setting the restaurant concept, financial strategy, culture, and standards. May be owner-operator or separate ownership and management.

roles.title: Owner / Operator
roles.description: Ultimate authority for the restaurant; sets concept, brand, financial targets, and major strategic decisions. May also serve as GM or Executive Chef in smaller operations.

roles.title: General Manager
roles.description: Senior operational leader overseeing both front and back of house; manages P&L, staffing, guest experience standards, and vendor relationships.

roles.title: Restaurant Manager
roles.description: Supports the GM in daily operations; handles shift management, opening/closing procedures, inventory, and staff scheduling.

roles.title: Sommelier / Beverage Director
roles.description: Curates wine list and beverage program; trains staff on wine service, manages cellar inventory, and assists guests with pairings.

departments.name: Back of House / Kitchen Brigade
departments.description: Heart of the restaurant operation; creates the menu, preps ingredients, and executes every dish to standard during service. Led by the Executive Chef with Sous Chefs as lieutenants and Chefs de Partie owning specific stations such as saute, grill, pastry, and cold kitchen.

roles.title: Executive Chef
roles.description: Creates the menu, sets culinary standards, manages kitchen budget and food cost, hires kitchen staff, and oversees all food output. The senior culinary authority.

roles.title: Head Chef / Chef de Cuisine
roles.description: Runs the kitchen day-to-day; manages service, enforces recipes and plating standards, oversees all stations, and handles kitchen administration.

roles.title: Sous Chef
roles.description: Second-in-command in the kitchen; expedites during service, trains junior cooks, manages inventory and ordering, and covers any station as needed.

roles.title: Junior Sous Chef
roles.description: Supports the Sous Chef with line management and service execution; typically responsible for specific sections or shifts.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Saute)
roles.description: Owns the saute station: pan-frying, searing, and finishing proteins and sauces over high heat. Must work fast and precisely under pressure.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Grill)
roles.description: Operates the grill station; responsible for cooking meats, fish, and vegetables over open flame or plancha to precise doneness specifications.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Garde Manger)
roles.description: Runs the cold kitchen: salads, cold appetizers, charcuterie, terrines, and cold plated dishes. Also responsible for pantry organization.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Pastry)
roles.description: Creates all desserts, baked goods, breads, and pastry components. May work separate hours from the main line.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Entremetier)
roles.description: Manages vegetable, starch, and egg dishes; often prepares soups, stocks, and hot appetizers as well.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Poissonnier)
roles.description: Specialist fish station; handles all seafood preparation and cooking including filleting, scaling, and precise fish cookery.

roles.title: Chef de Partie (Tournant)
roles.description: Float/swing cook who can work any station; fills in for absences and covers the busiest sections during peak service.

roles.title: Commis / Line Cook
roles.description: Entry-level kitchen position; assists the station's Chef de Partie with prep, mise en place, basic cooking tasks, and cleanup. Primary path to advancing in the brigade.

roles.title: Kitchen Porter / Dishwasher
roles.description: Maintains kitchen cleanliness, washes dishes and equipment, stocks supplies, and supports the kitchen team with basic prep and waste management.

departments.name: Front of House
departments.description: Responsible for the entire guest-facing experience from arrival, seating, service, and departure. Sets the tone and pace of the dining experience and directly impacts guest satisfaction and revenue.

roles.title: Head Server / Captain
roles.description: Leads the service team during shifts; assigns sections, briefs on menu specials, handles VIP tables, and manages the flow of the floor.

roles.title: Server / Waiter
roles.description: Primary guest contact: takes orders, describes menu items, delivers food and beverages, handles payment, and ensures guest satisfaction throughout the meal.

roles.title: Server Assistant / Busser
roles.description: Supports servers by clearing tables, refilling water, polishing silverware, resetting tables, and assisting with runner duties.

roles.title: Expediter / Announcer
roles.description: Bridges kitchen and front-of-house; calls out finished plates, checks plating quality, communicates modifications, and manages ticket timing.

roles.title: Food Runner
roles.description: Delivers finished plates from kitchen pass to the correct tables; communicates special requests and ensures hot food arrives immediately.

roles.title: Host / Maitre d'Hotel
roles.description: Manages reservations, greets guests upon arrival, seats parties, controls dining room flow, and manages wait times.

roles.title: Bartender
roles.description: Prepares and serves alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages; manages bar inventory, creates cocktail menus, and may serve bar-top guests directly.

roles.title: Barback
roles.description: Supports bartenders by restocking liquor, ice, and garnishes; cleans glassware, maintains bar cleanliness, and assists with keg changes.

departments.name: Support / Admin
departments.description: Non-service staff that keep the business running: accounting, marketing, HR, and facilities management. Often shared across multiple locations in larger restaurant groups.

roles.title: Restaurant Administrator
roles.description: Handles payroll, accounts payable/receivable, vendor payments, and financial reporting. May also manage HR records and compliance.

roles.title: Marketing Coordinator
roles.description: Manages social media, email campaigns, event promotion, PR relationships, and local advertising to drive traffic and brand awareness.

roles.title: Facilities / Maintenance
roles.description: Maintains all restaurant equipment, HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems; manages repairs and vendor maintenance contracts.

key_relationships: Executive Chef and General Manager meet daily to align on food cost, labor targets, guest feedback, and operational issues.
Chef de Cuisine and Sous Chefs communicate constantly during service via the expo line to coordinate timing across all stations.
Expediter bridges front and back of house, communicating modifications, dietary restrictions, and service pace between the kitchen and serving team.
Sous Chef and Head Server coordinate on table timing and pacing to ensure the kitchen can handle the volume of incoming orders.
Chef de Partie and their Commis have a mentorship dynamic typical of the brigade system, with on-the-job training and skill progression.
Sommelier coordinates with both the kitchen (food pairings) and the service team (wine recommendations and service standards).
Bartender and Barback work in tandem during service, with the barback ensuring the bartender never runs out of stock.
Kitchen Porter and all Chefs de Partie depend on each other: cooks need clean equipment and the porter needs proper scraping and sorting from cooks.
